Your members will be asked about their satisfaction regarding coaching, technical services, facilities, individual player feedback, training, match day experience, etc. This area will be scored using the Net Promoter Score methodology and results collected and processed by FQ.

The feedback will be uploaded into the club’s CDU folder at the conclusion of the Club Development & Assessment year.

Minimum number of responses to be evaluated in each timepoint: 30

The Average NPS scoring breakdown is as follows:

• NPS >= 30 = 3 points

• 20 =<  NPS < 30 = 2.5 points

• 15 =<  NPS < 20 = 2 points

• 10 =<  NPS < 15 = 1.5 point

• 5 =<  NPS < 10 = 1 point

• 0 =<  NPS < 5 = 0.5 point

• NPS <0 = 0 points

name: Shared Best Practice Delivery
evidence: Practical or Theory Delivery, Or Submission Evidence
criteria:
Clubs can score in two ways. Gold-rated Clubs will be provided the opportunity to share their knowledge and present a Shared Best Practice (SBP) webinar or workshop upon meeting the following criteria:

The nominated item should be a point of difference for the Club – unique and specific.

The nominated item must have been awarded the highest score (3 points) in the previous year’s assessment.

The workshop/webinar should be presented by Lead Technical Staff or Club Officials (TD, coach, etc.) or a qualified specialist provider within the February–July window.

Gold-rated Clubs may also opt to complete their SBP via TD mentoring. These Clubs must follow the template provided in their Club Development Plan and mentor at least one Pool B or C Club Technical Director. The process must document:

Initial meeting and information sharing with the mentored Club TD.

Mentee Club TD’s training visit to observe the program’s delivery on a training night.

Mentee Club TD attendance at one of the Gold Club’s internal coach education workshops or events.

If all three steps are completed and documented with dates and content, full points will be awarded.

name: Female Technical Staff
criteria:
In line with the Football Australia and FQ strategic target of 50/50 gender parity, this item assesses the current percentage of female technical staff holding positions at the club.

The club is required to list all coaching staff and their current valid qualifications as part of the Technical Staff Qualification submission via the template located in the Club's folder in the FQ Club Development Hub.

The female technical staff scoring breakdown is as follows:

Percentage >= 35% = 3 points

25% =< percentage < 35% = 2.5 points

20% =< percentage < 25% = 2 points

15% =< percentage < 20% = 1.5 point

10% =< percentage < 15% = 1 point

0% < percentage < 10% = 0 points

name: Female Participation
criteria:
In line with the Football Australia and FQ strategic target of 50/50 gender parity, this item assesses the current percentage of female players at the club in relation to the overall player base along with the growth of female participation from 2026 > 2027. Club scores are calculated by taking the state's average participation and player growth into account.

No submission is required as scores will be calculated based on player registration data recorded in Squadi. Clubs should ensure all players are correctly registered, as failure to register players correctly may result in a discrepancy in scoring.

name: Club Disciplinary Performance
criteria:
The club demonstrates a consistent commitment to fostering a positive, respectful, and safe match day environment focused on development for players, coaches, technical staff, team officials, and spectators. The club actively promotes behaviours that align with Football Queensland’s and the clubs, values, codes of conduct, and competition regulations.

Assessment will consider the club's overall disciplinary record across all Academy teams, including yellow cards, red cards, misconduct reports, suspended matches, and monetary fines issued throughout the season. The objective is to encourage positive touchline behaviours, respect for match officials, opponents, and the game, while reducing incidents that negatively impact the football environment that detract from learning.

The club's end-of-season disciplinary record should demonstrate a commitment to maintaining standards that are at or above Football Queensland benchmarks. Consistently low levels of disciplinary sanctions may indicate that positive behavioural expectations are embedded across the club's football program.

As part of the induction processes it is recommended that the club educates players, coaches, technical staff, and team officials on expected behaviours and takes proactive measures to minimise misconduct throughout the season. The club should implement strategies that promote self-discipline, emotional control, respect, accountability, and positive role modelling from players, coaches, and technical staff.

Note: Any offences or disciplinary actions occurring after the scores have been confirmed will be considered in the following year's assessment.

name: Fee Transparency
criteria: The club is required to provide a breakdown of fees using the FQ template to ensure comparability across all clubs. Additionally, it must provide a statement confirming that all academy development fees are exclusively used to support the club’s academy program

name: Scholarship positions
criteria: The club is required to provide a list of players who have received a full or partial scholarship for the current season, in accordance with the licence agreement (if applicable).

name: Coaches Registration
criteria:
All club coaches across all programs must be registered in Squadi, the official system for the season. Registration for coaches is free of charge.

As part of the Technical Staff Qualification submission, the club is required to provide a list containing all coaches' details and their team allocations.

name: Fielding teams and squad numbers
criteria: The club is required to provide a complete list of players by the deadline set by FQ before the season commences. If the squad list is incomplete or changes occur, regular updates must be provided to FQ's Competition and Technical Department. All teams must be fielded in accordance with the licence agreement.

name: Technical Director Qualification
criteria:
Tier 1 Club Technical Directors must hold or be enrolled in the current season in the AFC/Football Australia 'A' Diploma or Licence, or an overseas equivalent. The Technical Director must reside in Queensland to attend training, games, meetings, and fulfil club duties.

While the qualification remains a key requirement, Football Queensland recognises that other factors may contribute to a Technical Director's suitability for the role. These include previous experience as a Technical Director, coaching experience, the level of support provided by the club, the club's technical environment, and equity considerations.

Any request for an exemption or consideration of exceptional circumstances will be assessed on a case-by-case basis, at the sole discretion of FQ, taking into account the supporting documentation and evidence provided by the club. An exemption is not automatic and will only be considered where sufficient justification is demonstrated.

name: Safeguarding (Blue Cards)
criteria: As part of the Technical Staff Qualification submission, the club is required to provide a list including the full names, Blue Card numbers, and expiry dates of all coaches, support staff, and administrators involved in the academy program. The template provided by FQ must be used for this submission.

name: Club Structure Standards
criteria: The club is required to submit the organisational structure, position descriptions, and staff roster/contact information for teams. The club structure standards are set for each shield level and have been progressively introduced over a four-year period. Please refer to pages titled ‘Shield Thresholds’ within the Club Development & Assessment Info Pack for additional details on standards and submission requirements per shield.

name: Coaching Standards
criteria: The club is required to meet minimum coaching qualification and staffing standards per shield. Qualification standards are captured in each club’s Technical Staff Qualifications template and do not require a separate submission. To capture staffing standards, clubs must submit the names and roster of secondary coaches at the beginning of the season. Compliance with the above will be recorded during CDA’s training delivery observations. The coaching standards are set for each shield level and have been progressively introduced over a four-year period. Please refer to pages titled ‘Shield Thresholds’ within the Club Development & Assessment Info Pack for additional details on standards and submission requirements per shield.

name: Training Program Standards
criteria: Training Program Standards capture clubs' ability to provide players with a minimum requirement for frequency and duration of training sessions per week, appropriate field space, and individualised training sessions. Compliance with Training Standards will be evaluated through various means, primarily during training delivery observations. The club is required to submit their full training schedule with field allocation, as per previous years. The training program standards are set for each shield level and have been progressively introduced over a four-year period. Please refer to pages titled ‘Shield Thresholds’ within the Club Development & Assessment Info Pack for additional details on standards and submission requirements per shield.
